title: Harrison Price's site study picks Anaheim
description: Walt and Roy Disney hire the Stanford Research Institute; economist Harrison "Buzz" Price compares ten Southern California sites and recommends a 160-acre orange grove in Anaheim.

title: Disneyland opens with the first hub-and-spoke park plan
description: A single entrance, Main Street, a central plaza and lands radiating from it set the template for most later theme parks.

title: Kevin Lynch publishes The Image of the City
description: Paths, edges, districts, nodes and landmarks become the standard vocabulary for legible places, later borrowed by park planners.

title: Reedy Creek Improvement District created
description: Florida's governor signs the act giving Disney's Florida resort its own utility, building-code and fire powers.

title: Fruin publishes Pedestrian Planning and Design
description: John J. Fruin introduces the pedestrian level-of-service scale used to size walkways and queues.

title: Magic Kingdom opens above its utilidors
description: Service corridors built at ground level, with the park raised on lagoon fill, keep cast and deliveries out of sight.

title: Hillier and Hanson publish The Social Logic of Space
description: The founding text of space syntax, which predicts movement from the shape of a path network.

title: Universal Studios Florida opens around a lagoon
description: Themed areas arranged around a central lagoon establish the loop layout as the main alternative to the hub.

title: Ferrari World Abu Dhabi opens
description: A mostly indoor park under one roof shows how hot-climate sites move the whole park inside.

title: Warner Bros. World Abu Dhabi opens
description: A fully enclosed, air-conditioned park with six themed areas, later recognised as the world's largest indoor theme park.

title: Universal Epic Universe opens
description: A new hub-and-spoke park: Celestial Park at the centre, four portal worlds, about 110 acres inside a 750-acre site held for expansion.
